units.source_text: “五十年来，我习惯正襟危坐，盘腿反而觉得痛苦了。

en.t: For fifty years, I have been used to sitting upright and formal; now sitting cross-legged feels painful instead.

units.source_text: 在医院净躺在病榻上，回到家中，现时还不能端坐。

en.t: In the hospital I did nothing but lie in bed, and even after returning home, I still cannot sit upright now.

units.source_text: 用饭时，把桌布搭在前面，盘腿坐下后把腿藏起来。

en.t: At meals, I drape the tablecloth in front of me, sit cross-legged, and hide my legs underneath.

units.source_text: 与其说盘腿，不如说将两条细腿伸了出去。

en.t: Rather than saying I sit cross-legged, it would be more accurate to say I stretch out my two thin legs.

units.source_text: 过去从未有过这种动作。

en.t: I had never made such a movement before.

units.source_text: 我不能长时间端坐，这同对手下棋就不好办了。

en.t: Since I cannot sit upright for long, playing a game of go with an opponent becomes difficult.

units.source_text: 我在努力恢复正坐姿势，还不能说很有把握。”

en.t: I am trying to regain the proper seated posture, but I still cannot say I am very confident.”
